record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.original_question: Let M be an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group has non-trivial center. Does M admit a finite covering space with a non-trivial S1-action?

evidence.quote: If M is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group has a non-trivial center, is there a finite covering which admits a non-trivial S1-action?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a closed aspherical manifold (i.e., a closed manifold whose universal cover is contractible), and assume that the center $Z(\pi_1(M))$ of its fundamental group is non-trivial. Does there exist a finite covering space $\widetilde{M} \to M$ such that $\widetilde{M}$ admits a non-trivial continuous action of the circle group $S^1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The original Conner–Raymond conjecture, asserting that $M$ itself admits a non-trivial $S^1$-action, was disproved by Cappell–Weinberger–Yan, who constructed closed aspherical manifolds in all dimensions greater than 7 with non-trivial center in the fundamental group but admitting no topological circle action. The weaker version asking only for such an action on some finite cover is still listed as an open problem in current surveys on aspherical manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Closed Aspherical Manifolds with Center
status_evidence.snippet: In all dimensions greater than 7 there are closed aspherical manifolds whose fundamental groups have nontrivial center but do not possess any topological circle actions.
status_evidence.claim: The strong form of the Conner–Raymond conjecture (an S^1-action on M itself) is false.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds (Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: If M is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group has a non-trivial center, is there a finite covering which admits a non-trivial S^1-action?
status_evidence.claim: The finite-cover version of the question is recorded as an open problem.
